title: Overnight Pumpkin Spice French Toast Bake
changes_from_base: A bake-ahead version: challah slices soak overnight in a milk custard spiced with a home-made pumpkin spice mix (no pumpkin), then bake under foil and finish uncovered.
summary: Spiced bread baked overnight in a warming custard until puffed and golden, served with maple syrup and fresh raspberries.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm baking dish (metal, glass or ceramic)

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cut into small cubes, plus a little for the dish
fine sea salt or table salt
challah or brioche loaf, in 2 cm slices
fresh raspberries or other berries, to serve (optional)

steps.title: Spice
steps.text: Combine 2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp ginger, ½ tsp nutmeg, ¼ tsp allspice and ¼ tsp cloves to make the spice blend.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 480 ml milk with 4 eggs, 50 g brown sugar, the spice blend, 1 tsp vanilla and ½ tsp salt.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Dip each slice of the 450 g challah or brioche loaf into the custard and arrange in slightly overlapping rows in a buttered 23 x 33 cm dish, then pour over the rest.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover with foil and refrigerate overnight.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: The next day, turn each slice so the wetter side faces up, dot with 42 g butter cubes, cover with foil and bake at 175 °C (155 °C fan) for 15 min.

steps.title: Finish baking
steps.text: Uncover and bake for a further 15-20 min until lightly browned, slightly puffed and the centre reads 71 °C, tenting with foil if it browns too quickly.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool briefly, then serve with 80 ml maple syrup and 125 g fresh raspberries.

tips: Mix the ground spices together before whisking them into the custard so the pumpkin spice spreads evenly with no clumps.
Overlapping the slices evenly helps the bake set without any dry patches.
Tent with foil if the top is browning faster than the centre is cooking.
Preparing the custard the night before means less to do on the morning you serve it.
storage: Covered in the fridge, leftovers keep for up to two days; reheat in the oven until warmed through. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
